goals: Verify arithmetic correctness independently of the RTL implementation.
Verify control protocol, latency, reset behavior and divide-by-zero behavior.
Exercise important operand/result classes and record functional coverage.
Use bounded formal properties to supplement simulation.
Use mutation testing to evaluate the quality of the verification environment.
Carry the same methodology into SKY130 physical implementation and later Radix-4/Radix-8 comparisons.

tests.objective: Exercise boundary values that random stimulus can easily miss.
tests.stimulus: Directed vectors including zero, equality, max values, divisor=1 and other boundary relationships.
tests.oracle: Python mathematical reference model plus N = Q*D + R and unsigned remainder bound.
tests.pass_criteria: Every directed transaction matches quotient, remainder and DBZ expectations.
tests.why_it_matters: Boundary comparisons are common divider bug locations; this test killed the strict-comparator mutation.
tests.failure_indicates: Arithmetic boundary handling, result capture, or protocol contamination may be incorrect.

tests.objective: Exercise a broad operand space with a reproducible seed.
tests.oracle: Python mathematical reference model and arithmetic invariants.
tests.pass_criteria: All generated transactions match the reference model.
tests.why_it_matters: Broadens arithmetic exploration while retaining reproducibility.
tests.failure_indicates: A general arithmetic or state-machine defect may exist.

tests.objective: Verify the architectural latency contract and one-cycle completion pulse.
tests.stimulus: A normal non-DBZ transaction while counting clock iterations.
tests.oracle: For WIDTH=32, completion must occur after exactly 32 radix-2 iterations and done must not remain asserted.
tests.pass_criteria: Exact expected latency and one-cycle done behavior.
tests.why_it_matters: Arithmetic can be correct while the interface protocol is unusable; this test detects that distinction.
tests.failure_indicates: Counter termination, completion timing, or done-pulse logic is wrong.

tests.oracle: DBZ=1, quotient=all ones, remainder=dividend, immediate deterministic completion.
tests.pass_criteria: All DBZ outputs and timing match the specified convention.
tests.why_it_matters: Exceptional behavior must be specified and repeatable rather than left undefined.
tests.failure_indicates: DBZ detection, result convention, or immediate-completion protocol is incorrect.

tests.objective: Ensure a second request cannot corrupt an in-flight division.
tests.stimulus: Assert a new start while busy is already high.
tests.oracle: The active transaction must complete with its original operands/result.
tests.pass_criteria: Second start is ignored and active operation remains correct.
tests.why_it_matters: Checks transaction ownership and protects state from illegal/redundant requests.
tests.failure_indicates: Handshake gating or internal operand/state retention is defective.

tests.objective: Verify reset cancels an in-flight operation and returns the DUT to idle.
tests.stimulus: Start a division, assert reset before completion, then inspect interface state.
tests.oracle: Busy/done/state return to the defined reset values with no stale completion.
tests.pass_criteria: Operation is cancelled and reset state is restored deterministically.
tests.why_it_matters: Real systems reset asynchronously to transaction progress; stale state is a common integration failure.
tests.failure_indicates: Reset coverage of state/registers or transaction cancellation is incomplete.

tests.objective: Exercise and require important operand/result classes, not merely a vector count.
tests.stimulus: Directed cases plus deterministic random transactions.
tests.oracle: Every transaction is scoreboard-checked; coverage bins are recorded independently.
tests.pass_criteria: All required functional bins hit (current target: 11/11) and every transaction is correct.
tests.why_it_matters: Shows what semantic spaces were exercised and exposes holes hidden by raw random counts.
tests.failure_indicates: Either a functional mismatch occurred or the planned stimulus space is not closed.

tests.objective: Validate the independent bit-accurate Radix-2 Python algorithm against mathematical division.
tests.oracle: Mathematical //, %, DBZ convention and arithmetic invariants.
tests.pass_criteria: No generated counterexample separates the two Python models.
tests.why_it_matters: Reduces the chance that the algorithmic reference itself contains an unnoticed defect.
tests.failure_indicates: The algorithmic reference and mathematical specification disagree; RTL conclusions should pause.

tests.objective: Prevent an invalid interface state where busy and done conflict.
tests.stimulus: Symbolic state/input exploration within the BMC depth.
tests.pass_criteria: No counterexample within the configured bound.
tests.why_it_matters: Checks a control invariant over all symbolic values explored by the solver.
Complements directed DBZ simulation with symbolic exploration.
tests.failure_indicates: DBZ semantics are not invariant under the explored states.

tests.objective: Check N = Q*D + R at completion.
tests.stimulus: Symbolic dividend/divisor within the small formal configuration.
tests.oracle: Widened arithmetic assertion in the formal harness.
tests.why_it_matters: This is the central mathematical identity of quotient/remainder division.
tests.failure_indicates: Completed arithmetic result violates the mathematical specification.

tests.objective: Check unsigned remainder is smaller than the divisor for non-DBZ completion.
tests.why_it_matters: The identity alone can allow non-canonical quotient/remainder pairs; the bound disambiguates them.

tests.objective: Demonstrate the formal harness can reach divide-by-zero completion.
tests.why_it_matters: Guards against a vacuous harness that never reaches DBZ completion.
tests.failure_indicates: The scenario may be unreachable under assumptions or the cover depth is insufficient.

tests.why_it_matters: Provides evidence the bounded environment reaches the state where arithmetic assertions matter.
tests.failure_indicates: Harness/assumption/depth problem or unreachable normal completion.

tests.objective: Check layout geometry against foundry design rules.
tests.why_it_matters: A logically correct design is not manufacturable if geometric rules are violated.

tests.objective: Check that extracted layout connectivity matches the intended netlist.
tests.stimulus: Final layout extraction versus schematic/netlist view.
tests.why_it_matters: Proves layout connectivity is consistent with the design netlist.
tests.failure_indicates: Physical connectivity differs from the intended circuit.

tests.objective: Check/repair antenna-rule risks introduced during routing.
tests.why_it_matters: Protects gate oxides against manufacturing charge accumulation.
tests.failure_indicates: Routing requires antenna repair or remains non-compliant.
